settings: BONOBO.bonobo_output_format: File type of the per-sample matrices: .h5 or .hdf (HDF5), .txt or .csv.
BONOBO.sample_names: Explicit sample IDs; never positional sample indices.
BONOBO.sparsify: Compute approximate edge p-values and threshold each sample's co-expression matrix at bonobo_confidence (with save_pvals, the full matrix is kept and the p-values are written).
BONOBO.bonobo_confidence: Significance level at which sparsify thresholds the edges.
BONOBO.save_pvals: Write each sample's edge p-value matrix; requires sparsify.
BONOBO.precision: Floating-point precision: single or double.
BONOBO.keep_in_memory: Keep the per-sample matrices in memory during the run (upstream run_bonobo option).
BONOBO.delta: Weight of the sample in its covariance; empty estimates it per sample. With sparsify it must be above 0 and below 1/3 (Log 224).
BONOBO.genes_axis: Where the gene IDs are in the expression table: auto, rows or columns (BONOBO needs them on rows).
BONOBO.log_transformed: The expression is declared log-transformed; BONOBO requires it.
BONOBO.centered: The expression is declared centered; BONOBO requires it.
CONDOR.prefix: Prefix for derived CONDOR artifacts.
DRAGON.output_format: matrix: a labeled symmetric partial-correlation matrix; edge_list: one row per feature pair (source, target, partial_correlation, precision).

DRAGON.lambda1: Shrinkage of omics layer 1 (DRAGON's layer-specific shrinkage, not a generic graphical-lasso or sparsity penalty). Empty estimates it; a manual value needs lambda1 and lambda2 together, both in [0, 1].

DRAGON.lambda2: Shrinkage of omics layer 2 (DRAGON's layer-specific shrinkage, not a generic graphical-lasso or sparsity penalty). Empty estimates it; a manual value needs lambda1 and lambda2 together, both in [0, 1].

LIONESS-DRAGON.lambda1: Shrinkage of omics layer 1 (DRAGON's layer-specific shrinkage, not a generic graphical-lasso or sparsity penalty). Empty estimates it once on all samples; a manual value needs lambda1 and lambda2 together, both in [0, 1].

LIONESS-DRAGON.lambda2: Shrinkage of omics layer 2 (DRAGON's layer-specific shrinkage, not a generic graphical-lasso or sparsity penalty). Empty estimates it once on all samples; a manual value needs lambda1 and lambda2 together, both in [0, 1].
OTTER.output_format: matrix: a labeled TF-by-gene matrix; edge_list: a complete source,target,weight TF-to-gene grid.
OTTER.computing: Hardware the optimization runs on: cpu or gpu.
OTTER.precision: Floating-point precision of the optimization: single or double.
OTTER.lam: Weight of gene co-expression versus the TF-TF PPI network in OTTER's fit, as (lam, 1 - lam); not a sparsity penalty.
OTTER.gamma: L2-style regularization of the TF-gene matrix W; not a sparsity penalty or threshold.
OTTER.iterations: Number of optimization iterations.
OTTER.eta: Step size (learning rate) of OTTER's gradient optimization.
OTTER.bexp: Exponent used in OTTER's optimization updates; it controls the optimization, not regularization.
PANDA.with_header: Expression input has a header.
SAMBAR.norm_patient: Normalize gene mutation scores by each patient's mutation burden.
SAMBAR.kmin: Smallest number of sample subtypes (clusters) tried; at least 2.
SAMBAR.kmax: Largest number of sample subtypes (clusters) tried; at least kmin and at most the number of samples.
SAMBAR.gmt_msigdb: The pathway GMT file is in MSigDB format.
SAMBAR.subset_cancer_genes: Score only the listed cancer-associated genes.
SAMBAR.distance: Distance (a scipy metric name) between samples' pathway scores used for clustering.
SAMBAR.linkage: Hierarchical-clustering linkage method (a scipy name).
SAMBAR.cluster: Cluster samples into subtypes; false returns the mutation scores only.

produces.text: One weighted TF-to-gene regulatory network across all the samples given.
Each TF's out-degree and each gene's in-degree (targeting scores) in that network.
Which edges or TF targeting scores differ between conditions.
One weighted network of how TFs and miRNAs regulate genes, across all samples.
Each regulator's out-degree and each gene's in-degree.
One TF-gene network per sample, plus the aggregate network.
A TF-by-sample (or gene-by-sample) targeting-score matrix.
Edges or targeting scores tested between groups, paired time points, or against clinical variables (e.g. survival).
One TF/miRNA-gene network per sample, plus the aggregate network.
A TF-by-sample (or gene-by-sample) targeting-score matrix.
Edges or targeting scores tested between groups, paired time points, or against clinical variables (e.g. survival).
One weighted TF-to-gene regulatory network across all samples, fitted so that it agrees with the PPI network and gene co-expression.
Each TF's out-degree and each gene's in-degree (targeting scores) in that network.
A signed TF-to-gene regulatory matrix (positive activating, negative repressing), across all samples.
Each TF's activity in each sample, estimated apart from its own mRNA level.
TF activity tested between conditions or against clinical variables.
One undirected partial-correlation network within and between two matched omics layers (any two, e.g. expression and methylation), across all samples.
A p-value and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value for every edge (adjusted within each layer and across the layers), to filter edges by significance.
Cross-layer edges compared between groups.
One two-layer partial-correlation network per sample, plus the aggregate.
Per-sample edges compared between groups or individuals.
One gene-gene co-expression network per sample, plus the aggregate.
Per-sample gene degree or edge weights compared across samples or groups.
One gene-gene co-expression network per sample, estimated with a Bayesian model; optionally per-edge p-values per sample.
The part of each gene pair's co-expression associated with each covariate in a design matrix (e.g. group, batch), and a covariate-adjusted co-expression matrix.
A regulatory network built from batch-adjusted co-expression.
Communities in one bipartite network, with regulator-side and gene-side memberships, by bipartite modularity.
Each regulator's and gene's core score -- its share of its community's modularity -- to pick out each community's core nodes.
Pathway enrichment of each community's genes.

Patient subtypes from somatic mutations -- gene mutation scores summarized into pathway mutation scores, then hierarchical clustering of the patients on them -- with the scores, the cluster labels and the sample distance matrix.
Subtypes compared with clinical variables such as survival.

near_miss.text: Which TFs physically form complexes, or complex stoichiometry.
near_miss.why_not: The PPI network is an input of possible TF cooperation. PANDA refines a cooperativity matrix internally, but the executor does not save it, and it is not a measurement of physical complexes or stoichiometry.

near_miss.text: Whether a TF activates or represses a gene.
near_miss.why_not: Edge weights are unsigned support scores.

near_miss.text: Discover a TF's binding motif or binding sites.
near_miss.why_not: The motif prior is an input; PANDA never searches sequence.

near_miss.text: A model of how expression or regulation evolves over time.
near_miss.why_not: One static network per set of samples; time points can only be compared as separate networks.

near_miss.text: lncRNA regulators, ceRNA or miRNA-sponge networks.
near_miss.why_not: PUMA's non-TF regulators are miRNAs given by a target prior; it has no lncRNA layer and models no sponging.

near_miss.text: miRNA-gene edges estimated from miRNA expression (e.g. anti-correlation).
near_miss.why_not: The miRNA's own expression is not an input.

near_miss.text: Networks for individual cells.
near_miss.why_not: Built for bulk samples; per-cell co-expression is dominated by dropout.

near_miss.text: Which gene pairs differ significantly between groups.

near_miss.text: Fine-mapping causal variants, or variant effects on binding.
near_miss.why_not: CONDOR partitions a given network; it does not test or fine-map variants (its original eQTL use takes eQTL associations as input).

near_miss.text: Subtypes from expression, methylation or other non-mutation data.
near_miss.why_not: SAMBAR's input is somatic mutations.

near_miss.text: Which mutations are drivers, or mutation calling.
near_miss.why_not: SAMBAR summarizes given mutation calls; it does not call or rank driver mutations.

registry_wide.text: Proof that one thing causes another (causal drivers, causal direction of an edge, ruling out confounding).
registry_wide.why_not: Every registered workflow estimates associations or model coefficients from observational data.

registry_wide.text: A trained model that predicts an outcome, a future state or a perturbation effect, with its accuracy.
registry_wide.why_not: No registered workflow fits a predictive or generative model; per-sample results can only be features for one built elsewhere.

registry_wide.text: Results sent, uploaded, published or shown to anyone outside the analysis (e-mail, a public or shared database or repository, a website, a dashboard or app).
registry_wide.why_not: Every registered workflow writes result files to the output folder you give; sending, uploading, publishing or showing them is done outside NetZoo.
